note: Byte-parity vectors for the attachment-blob cipher. Layout: nonce(12) || ciphertext || tag(16), AAD empty, key 32 bytes — byte-for-byte libsignal Aes256GcmEncryptedData.concatenate(). Generated FROM THE APP SIDE (the app's own TacendumDev.crypto.blobEncrypt) — never from the CLI implementation under test, so parity is proven against the shipped side rather than a tautology. Every positive case has been round-tripped through the app's own blobDecrypt; the empty case was re-proven after the pod 0.98.0 empty-ciphertext crash was fixed (its bytes unchanged — see its appRoundTripNote). The nonce is pinned BY the fixture (first 12 blob bytes), so the CLI encrypt direction is checked byte-exactly, not just decrypt. Negative cases are derived from app-produced bytes and name which check must fire; the suite must refuse to certify parity if provenance.appSide is not true.

cases.name: empty
cases.appRoundTripNote: FIXED: app-side blobDecrypt crashed on this legal 28-byte blob (EXC_BREAKPOINT in libsignal Swift Aes256GcmDecryption.decrypt via Data.withUnsafeMutableBytes on empty ciphertext) — a pod 0.98.0 slice-handling defect, fixed by a non-slice guard in the app's blobDecrypt, then round-trip device-proven: this pinned empty vector decrypted in-app, tampered-empty rejected by throw. Bytes unchanged — the original app-side encrypt provenance stands.

negatives.name: flipped-tag-bit
negatives.detail: last byte of the 16-byte tag XOR 0x01 — GCM authentication must reject; no plaintext may escape

negatives.name: blob-27-bytes
negatives.detail: one byte under the 28-byte minimum (nonce 12 + tag 16) — the length check must fire before any cipher call

negatives.name: key-31-bytes
negatives.detail: a 31-byte key — the key-length assertion must fire before any cipher call
